Hi Anna / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call I put together three recommendation paths for a Dedicated (reserved) cluster that balance predictable latency, cost, and a practical ramp schedule tied to your upcoming pilot and production milestones. I attached the one-page PDF and the cost workbook; below is the short summary and the ask we need to move forward.

Summary (high-level options)

1) Pilot (Conservative) — 8 GPUs baseline, H100-equivalent (8 x H100-80GB), reserved 3mo.
   - Baseline throughput: ~120k prompt tokens / hour (concurrent short-chat workload)
   - Min-guaranteed GPUs: 6 (to give headroom for maintenance; billing at reserved level)
   - Autoscale burst to 16 GPUs for sustained peaks (burst capacity reserved but billed on commit rules)
   - Ramp: start 10/27 with 8 GPUs, monitor 2 weeks, scale to 12 if 30% utilization sustained

2) Growth (Balanced) — 16 GPUs baseline, H100/4-bit-friendly stack (quantized), reserved 6–12mo.
   - Baseline throughput: ~260k tokens / hour, smoother latency at 99th percentile
   - Min-guaranteed GPUs: 12
   - Autoscale burst to 32 GPUs for launches/peak hours (fast spin-up)
   - Ramp: start pilot 11/03 with 16; staged increases by 11/30 and 12/21 tied to traffic gates

3) Production (Aggressive / SLA-backed) — 32 GPUs baseline with multi-region standby (US-East + US-West).
   - Baseline throughput: >500k tokens / hour; 99.9% uptime SLA option
   - Min-guaranteed GPUs: 24 across regions
   - Autoscale: 64 GPUs burst possible during national campaigns
   - Ramp: 12-week ramp plan (counterpart runbooks + warm pool) — target cutover Q1 2027

Key notes / tradeoffs
- GPU SKUs: we recommend H100-80GB for large-context models; A100/Q4 stacks acceptable for quantized workloads with slightly different capacity math (see workbook).
- KV cache / pre-warm: to meet sub-200ms tails for chat we recommend pre-warmed KV caches and prefix caching for the most common flows. That requires reserving a small warm pool (we show 10% of baseline as a pragmatic number).
- Billing: reserved baseline billed monthly; burst usage billed per-minute when exceeding baseline (we included examples in the workbook).
- Data / compliance: Private deployment option (VPC) available if you want customer-managed network and KMS integration.

Attachments: SaturnHealth_ClusterSizing_Options_v1.pdf, saturn_capacity_costs.xlsx

Ask / next steps
- Please confirm which path you prefer for the SOW (Pilot / Growth / Production) and whether you want the multi-region standby option in scope.
- If Pilot: we can lock baseline and start cluster provisioning week of 10/27. Provisioning lead time for H100 hardware is ~5 business days after PO.
- If you want, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tue to walk the cost workbook with your finance/procurement team.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Rajiv / Anna — looping in a couple of technical specifics to address the questions below and make the SOW lines explicit.

1) Billing / min-guaranteed vs reserved baseline
- When you sign a reserved baseline (e.g., 8 GPUs), billing is at the reserved baseline rate. "Min-guaranteed" reflects the SLAs on how many hosts stay online during rolling maintenance or host failures; it is not a separate billable floor. If you reserve 8 but we guarantee 6 during maintenance windows, you still pay the reserved 8 monthly commitment. We can add a clause for credits if we miss agreed availability targets.

2) Burst/scale-up timing and warm pool
- Cold spin-up for physical GPUs (if provisioning new hosts) can be 3–5 minutes; our autoscaler uses a warm pool to reduce that to <10s for most workloads. Warm pool is effectively idle pre-warmed instances (partial KV cache warm) — recommended size: ~10% of baseline (we included line item).
- For H100 with our KV cache and prefix caching, tail latency growth is typically under 200–300ms when a warm pool is sized correctly. If you need <100ms tails we recommend >15% warm pool and more aggressive KV pre-population.

3) Multi-region recommendation
- For your profile (65% East), we recommend active-primary (US-East) + standby (US-West) active-passive with cross-region failover for cost efficiency. Active-active makes sense if you plan high geo-traffic or strict locality; it increases baseline GPUs because you must reserve capacity in both.

4) Context windows and GPU math
- 32k-context models increase KV cache and memory pressure. For H100-80GB you can comfortably run a moderate throughput serving node with 2–3 concurrent 32k calls depending on model size. We assumed 2 concurrent 32k calls per GPU for the capacity workbook. If you expect higher concurrency we should move the per-GPU concurrency assumption down (e.g., 1.2–1.5) which will raise GPU counts.

Attached: capacity-plan.xlsx (breaks down per-model memory, assumed concurrency, and warm-pool sizing). I've also updated the workbook with explicit SOW language for warm pool, crediting for provisioning delays, and burst billing terms.

If this looks good I can draft the SOW language and hand it to Rishi for pricing & credit terms.
